last.verdict: Berkshire's operating profit fell about 6% as insurance weakened, while it more than doubled buybacks to $9.6 billion and kept a $377 billion cash pile.

takeaways.label: Operating profit slipped
takeaways.text: Operating earnings fell 5.8% to $12.7 billion from $13.5 billion a year earlier, as insurance weakness outweighed gains at the railroad, utilities and manufacturing businesses.

takeaways.label: Insurance sharply weaker
takeaways.text: Insurance underwriting profit dropped 43% to $1.35 billion, and investment income from insurance float fell 14% to $2.7 billion, the main drag on the quarter.

takeaways.label: Buybacks accelerate
takeaways.text: Berkshire repurchased about $9.6 billion of its own stock, more than double the $4.5 billion in the prior quarter, bringing 2026 buybacks to roughly $14.4 billion.

takeaways.label: Cash still enormous
takeaways.text: Cash and Treasury bills rose 3% to $377.4 billion despite the buybacks. Net earnings fell 28% to $22.1 billion as investment gains roughly halved.

history.verdict: Investors cheered Berkshire finally spending its cash pile on buybacks and stocks.

reasons.label: Big share buybacks
reasons.text: Berkshire bought back about $4.5 billion of its own stock in the quarter, up from small buybacks before.

reasons.label: Cash put to work
reasons.text: Berkshire became a net stock buyer for the first time in about 14 quarters, with a Alphabet stake included.

reasons.label: Stronger operating profit
reasons.text: Operating earnings rose about 16% to $13.0 billion, though insurance underwriting profit slipped to $1.7 billion.
